newsitem.title: USA: British Telecom to buy MCI, CNBC says; stock halted.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom to buy MCI, CNBC says; stock halted.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc is in negotations to buy the remaining 80 percent of MCI Communications Corp. it does not already own, television channel CNBC said Friday.
Trading in MCI's stock was halted, the Nasdaq market said just after 1:30 p.m. EST.
"MCI ... is in negotiations to be bought by its 20 percent owner British Telecom, and sources close to the deal tell me it could be announced as early as Monday morning," a CNBC reporter said.
The stock jumped $5 to $30.625 after the CNBC report.

"It makes sense," said Kevin Haggerty, senior vice president and manager of equity trading at Fidelity Investments. "I think BT is a great company. The synergy is there. BT made a great initial investment."
Both companies, contacted by Reuters, had earlier declined to comment on the rumour, which had been circulating in the Nasdaq market. British Telecom currently owns 20 percent of MCI.
CNBC said Lazard Freres, MCI's investment bankers, and Morgan Stanley were working on the deal, which it said could be worth upward of $22 billion.
The reporter said that he had not been able to get the price of the deal, but one analyst had estimated MCI would be worth about $40 per share.
